english: The supreme Sound (nāda), whose essence is light (prakāśa), emerges as the seed of all energy (śakti).

devanagari: इडा च पिङ्गला चैव सुषुम्णा च तृतीयकाः
iast: iḍā ca piṅgalā caiva suṣumṇā ca tṛtīyakāḥ
english: Iḍā (lunar), Piṅgalā (solar), and Suṣumṇā (central) — these are the three principal nāḍīs (channels).

devanagari: ब्रह्मनाडीति सा प्रोक्ता सुषुम्णा या परा गतिः
iast: brahmanāḍīti sā proktā suṣumṇā yā parā gatiḥ
english: Suṣumṇā is called the Brahma-nāḍī (channel of the Absolute); it is the supreme path.
Kuṇḍalinī, the Great Power, resides in the Svādhiṣṭhāna (sacral cakra, at the base).
Mūlādhāra is the first cakra (root), Svādhiṣṭhāna the second (sacral).

iast: maṇipūraṃ tṛtīyaṃ syād anāhataṃ ca caturthakam
english: Maṇipūra (solar plexus) is the third, Anāhata (heart) the fourth.

iast: viśuddhaṃ pañcamaṃ proktam ājñācakraṃ tu ṣaṣṭhakam
english: Viśuddha (throat) is declared the fifth, Ājñā (third eye) the sixth.
Sahasrāra (crown) is the seventh, situated above all cakras.

iast: prāṇaḥ prāṇo apānaś ca vyānaś caiva samānakaḥ
english: The five prāṇas (vital breaths): Prāṇa, Apāna, Vyāna, Samāna, and Udāna.
These five are called the prāṇa-vāyus (vital airs), of which Udāna is the fifth.

iast: bhūmiḥ salilaṃ tejo vāyur ākāśam eva ca
english: Earth, Water, Fire, Air, and Ether — these are the five gross elements (mahābhūtas).
The elements dissolve (laya) into the tattvas progressively in reverse order — absorption into the source.
First sound (śabda), then meaning (artha); sound and meaning arise together.
Like the sound of a bell, the resonance shines forth in the Brahma-nāḍī (central channel).
Iḍā is of the nature of the moon (receptive), Piṅgalā is of the nature of the sun (active).

iast: ciñcinī cīrakārā ca ghaṇṭā tritayam īritam
english: Three sounds are described: ciñcinī (cricket-like, in Iḍā), cīra (cricket sound, in Piṅgalā), and ghaṇṭā (bell-like, in Suṣumṇā).
Prāṇāyāma has three aspects: Pūraka (inhalation), Recaka (exhalation), and Kumbhaka (retention).
In prāṇāyāma, retention (kumbhaka) should be four times the inhalation. The exhalation twice. This is the 1:4:2 ratio.

devanagari: यथा सिंहो गजो व्याघ्रो वश्यो भवति ताडितः
iast: yathā siṃho gajo vyāghro vaśyo bhavati tāḍitaḥ
english: Just as a lion, elephant, or tiger becomes controlled when struck, so the mind is controlled by the regulation of prāṇa.
Establishing meditation on the inner sound (nāda), one becomes filled with the bliss of the Absolute (brahmānanda).
